newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SPOTLIGHT FALLS ON ZOFF AS SACCHI IS PILLORIED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPOTLIGHT FALLS ON ZOFF AS SACCHI IS PILLORIED.

text.p: Former World Cup-winning goalkeeper Dino Zoff emerged as a front runner to take over as Italian coach on Thursday as the voices calling for Arrigo Sacchi to be dismissed grew after Italy's defeat by Bosnia.

The Rome daily newspaper Il Messaggero did not hide its disgust at the 2-1 result of Wednesday's friendly in Sarajevo, the first international there since the 44-month long war that killed 10,000 Sarajevans.
"Italian soccer in shame," a front page headline read, over a photograph of Sacchi holding his head.
"And now, please, kick them all out," it added.

Luciano Nizzola, league president and almost certain to be the next federation head after a December election, hinted heavily that Lazio chairman Zoff was in the frame, although it was by no means certain that Sacchi would go.
Asked whether Sacchi could be confident of being on the bench when Italy play England at Wembley in February in a key World Cup qualifier, Nizzola cut short any optimism.

"Nothing is certain," he was quoted as saying in the Corriere della Sera. "There is a problem and it will be faced calmly and seriously. For some time we have not been satisfied with the team, not even when the lads win."
Although polls show that a majority of Italians want Sacchi out, officials are caught in a dilemma.
If they fire Sacchi and his successor loses at Wembley they stand to be blamed for changing a coach who, while widely disliked, has won three out of three qualifiers.
But if they let Sacchi stay and Italy beat England their justification for replacing him could vanish.

Italian Olympic Committee head Mario Pescante called for Sacchi to be allowed to stay until Wembley while the Corriere dello Sport said it would be absurd to make a decision about Sacchi on the basis of a friendly.

"It was not a national team...it was hardly ever a match...let's be happy with the small show of solidarity brought to a people who have bigger problems than Sacchi's contract," the sports newspaper said.
But Nizzola appeared far from certain.
"We leaders are not happy, the fans are not happy and Sacchi himself is not happy," Nizzola was quoted as saying.
Nizzola said Sacchi's contract, which runs up to the 1998 World Cup in France, was not a major issue.
"We want to look after Italian soccer and create the best possible conditions to reach France," he said.
Nizzola said Zoff, who captained Italy's 1982 World Cup-winning team and won more caps than any other Italian player, was "one of the athletes who has given most to Italian soccer".
Zoff refused to comment on Nizzola's compliments on Thursday, beyond saying that "at the moment I'm only thinking of Lazio and its problems."
The three men seen as the main candidates to replace Saachi are:
Zoff -- played 112 times for Italy, won the league six times as a player with Juventus and described by Nizzola as "a national monument". No outstanding record as a coach.

Nevio Scala -- Cultured opera-loving former Parma coach who parted ways with Parma at the end of last season. Has never won a league title as a coach but took Parma to success in Europe with UEFA Cup win in 1995 and Cup Winners' Cup in 1993.

Cesare Maldini -- Former Italian captain and current under-21 coach, father of Italian captain Paolo. His star faded somewhat after Italy's poor showing at the Atlanta Olympics but has revived after recent matches.
